segments.text: I'm going to read the beginning of my Common App essay, which I've never shared before.
But this essay got me into 20 out of 26 schools, including Harvard, Stanford, and four other
IE's.
Hidden behind the white balustrades of a brand new home, I held my breath, watching
flecks of sunlight dance across the airy living room as I listened for my mother's
footsteps.
My grin stretched wider.
As a hide-and-seek enthusiast, transitioning from a cramped one-bedroom apartment to
a house replete with nooks and hallways was a dream come true.
I cherished the prickling sensation that would ascend my legs the longer I crashed the door
with scissors.
As a child, hiding was the thing I perfected.
But my ability to hide was not limited to the game.
And then my last paragraph was,
Abandoning my long-cherished role as a hider was uncomfortable at first, but unearthing
parts of myself was far more rewarding than any game of hide-and-seek.
Looking back, I am proud of my evolution from a silent assimilator into a fervent
advocate for childhood cancer research, healthcare equity, and women's rights.
I am now able to unequivocally accept who I am, one who seeks community, friendships,
and opportunities to pursue my love for making a difference.
Okay, I can get to a whole video about why I think that this common app essay worked.
It was definitely not my best writing or the most emotional, but I think there's
a strategy there which I can explain if you guys want to hear.
Bye guys, love you so much.
